hints: Notice the reagents, alkaline aqueous iodine is the classic test for one very specific group in a carbonyl compound.
Draw out 3-methylbutan-2-one as $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ and check if it contains a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ methyl ketone group.
Remember the methyl ketone is split, the $\text{CH}_3$ part becomes triiodomethane while the rest stays as a carboxylate that turns into a carboxylic acid on acidification.
walkthrough:
**Spot the iodoform reaction**

Great start, alkaline aqueous iodine means the triiodomethane (iodoform) reaction. It only works for methyl ketones, compounds containing the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$.

General reaction:
$$\text{R-CO-CH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Draw the ketone and find R**

Now let's look at our ketone. 3-methylbutanone is 3-methylbutan-2-one:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$
This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ joined to a $\text{-CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ group. So it is a methyl ketone and the reaction will happen. Here $\text{R} = (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-}$.

**Form the carboxylate then acidify**

In alkali, the R group becomes a carboxylate ion, $\text{R-COO}^-$:
$$ (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COO}^- $$
The question says the mixture is then acidified, so $\text{H}^+$ is added and the ion is protonated to the free acid:
$$ (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COO}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-COOH} $$
That is 2-methylpropanoic acid, named methylpropanoic acid.

options.A: This would be the product of simple oxidation with no carbon loss. The iodoform reaction cleaves off the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ methyl group as $\text{CHI}_3$, so the acid must be one carbon shorter than the starting ketone.
options.B: Butanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ with a straight 4-carbon chain. Our R group is branched, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-}$, so the acid formed must stay branched.
options.C: Correct and well done. The ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ undergoes the iodoform cleavage to give $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOO}^-$ plus $\text{CHI}_3$. Acidification gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$, which is methylpropanoic acid.
options.D: Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ with only 3 carbons in total. We lose only one carbon as $\text{CHI}_3$ from the 5-carbon ketone, so the acid product must have 4 carbons, not 3.
